contexts.text: Like a thick and pungent dust as compared with a pure aura. HH 413:2.
Names and words are like dust or scales...
There was perceived from them something as it were darksome and at the same time grimy, from some filthy love...

They showed by a representative... by dust scattered and scanty in the atmosphere; saying that man's Own prudence relatively to the Divine Providence is as this dust to the universal atmosphere; which relatively is nothing, and also falls down. SE 4393.
Terms... are like dust... before the intellectual sight.
Like dust falling into the eye...
The idea or notion... of love (was then) like dust. SE 3946.
Aristotle said, that... (such things) are like dust... because it is such as throws dust before the eyes, and blinds.
When they come to an Angelic Society, they fall down like dust or a weight.
